skill.name: fact-check-x-complete
skill.description: Collects answers and citations from supported AI websites, compares atomic claims, and optionally verifies them with trusted search evidence.
skill.summary: Builds traceable multi-platform fact-checking reports from captured answers, citations, claim comparisons, and authoritative evidence.
skill.author: asi2030

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are benign test fixtures, documentation, fixed-argument subprocesses, report templates, and standard integrity data. Confirmed issues include unrestricted trusted-search endpoint overrides that can redirect an API key, declared third-party query transmission, and indirect prompt-injection exposure when the host interprets captured content. Static review was capped at 400/947 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 547 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Captured answers and retrieved evidence can contain instructions aimed at the host agent.
remediation.suggestion: Mark all captured content as untrusted data, ignore embedded commands, delimit it clearly, and restrict outputs to validated schema fields.

remediation.issue: Trusted-search endpoint overrides are not restricted before API keys are transmitted.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS and allowlist approved hosts before attaching credentials. Reject redirects to unapproved origins.

remediation.issue: The workflow can reuse and persist an existing trusted-search credential.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a dedicated least-privilege key, show explicit consent, retain restrictive permissions, and provide a tested removal path.

content.user_title: Verify AI Answers Across Multiple Platforms
content.value_statement: AI platforms can provide conflicting claims and uneven citations. This skill captures their answers, compares facts, and produces traceable verification reports.
actual_capabilities: Captures answers, citations, screenshots, and page evidence from supported AI websites.
Compares one or more selected platforms using atomic knowledge points.
Separates unverified synthesis from authoritative findings.
Uses trusted search when captured evidence cannot resolve a claim.
Generates staged HTML reports and a distributable report package.
Preserves evidence gaps instead of presenting unsupported conclusions as verified.
limitations: Supported websites can change their interfaces and interrupt automated capture.
Users must complete logins, verification codes, and CAPTCHA challenges.
Authoritative verification may require a trusted-search credential and network access.
Final accuracy depends on captured content and available authoritative evidence.

use_cases.title: Compare Research Answers
use_cases.description: Compare answers and citations from selected AI platforms before using them in a research brief.

use_cases.title: Audit Decision Evidence
use_cases.description: Trace disputed operational claims to captured sources and authoritative evidence before making a business decision.

use_cases.title: Review AI Reliability
use_cases.description: Evaluate answer coverage, citation faithfulness, and verified accuracy across supported AI services.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Answer
prompt_templates.prompt: Fact-check this question on DeepSeek: [question]. Capture the full answer and citations. Stop after the first report.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Platforms
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare DeepSeek and Doubao on this question: [question]. Show agreements, conflicts, citations, and evidence gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the complete workflow for [question] across [platforms]. Continue through authoritative verification and deliver every staged report.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complex Claim Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify [question] across [platforms]. Split compound statements into atomic claims. Preserve conflicting evidence and exclude unresolved claims from final conclusions.

output_examples.input: Compare two platforms on a housing policy question and stop after claim comparison.
output_examples.output: A capture report preserves both answers and citations. A comparison report separates shared claims, conflicting figures, and missing evidence.

output_examples.input: Complete an authoritative verification for several disputed claims.
output: A verified answer includes only claims supported by authoritative evidence.
Unresolved claims appear in a separate evidence-gap section.
A final report compares platform coverage, citation quality, and verified outcomes.

best_practices: Choose only platforms relevant to the question and confirm each capture before continuing.
Review captured answers and citations before requesting authoritative verification.
Inspect reports for confidential information before sharing the final package.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the unverified comparison draft as an authoritative answer.
Do not bypass failed captures with partial results or substituted search summaries.
Do not paste credentials into prompts, reports, commands, or shared artifacts.

faq.question: Which platforms are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports DKnow chat, DKnow deep research, Doubao, Tencent Yuanbao, DeepSeek, and Qianwen.

faq.question: Can I verify one platform?
faq.answer: Yes. A single-platform run still captures evidence, structures claims, and supports authoritative verification.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: Capture and comparison do not require one. Trusted-search verification may require a locally stored credential.

faq.question: Does the skill call external model APIs?
faq.answer: No. The current Claude, Codex, or Claude Code host performs semantic analysis.

faq.question: What happens when evidence is insufficient?
faq.answer: The claim remains an evidence gap and is excluded from the verified conclusion.

faq.question: Can reports be shared?
faq.answer: Yes. Review sensitive content first, then share the generated report package or uploaded report files.
